name: KOSOVO

flag.title: Flag of Kosovo
flag.note: Blue field, gold map, six white stars

lead: Kosovo is Europe's newest country. It declared independence in 2008. Mountains ring it in the western Balkans. Its capital, Pristina, buzzes with cafés and street art. Its people are among Europe's youngest.

facts.label: Money
facts.sub: Uses EU currency, not in EU

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Kosovo is a bowl ringed by mountains. The Sharr range glitters in the south, and the Accursed Mountains rise in the west. Farmers grow wheat and peppers in the middle.
Kosovo has no coast. The nearest sea, the Adriatic, is about 200 km away. Clear mountain lakes and fast rivers make up for it.
animals: The Balkan lynx is a spotted wild cat with tufted ears. Only a few live in the Sharr Mountains. Each photo from a hidden camera is big news.
Brown bears, grey wolves and sure-footed chamois (mountain goats) roam the peaks. Golden eagles soar overhead. Albanian culture honours them.
culture: Kosovars love coffee and company. Friends share a tiny espresso in a Pristina café. Guests always get food. Saying no is thought rude!
At weddings, people link hands for the Valle, an Albanian circle dance. Prizren's silver filigree jewellery has been made by hand for over 500 years.
history: In the 13th and 14th centuries, Kosovo was the heart of the medieval Serbian Kingdom. In 1389, the Battle of Kosovo against the Ottoman Empire changed everything. Songs still remember it.
The Ottomans ruled for nearly 500 years. They left mosques, bazaars and stone bridges. Kosovo declared independence on 17 February 2008, with huge street parties.
wows: Kosovo declared independence in 2008, younger than many smartphones.
Pristina's giant NEWBORN sculpture gets a fresh design every independence day.
Kosovo uses the euro but is not in the EU.
A 6,000-year-old clay Goddess on the Throne was found near Pristina.
The Rahovec region has made wine since Roman times.
Over 70% of Kosovo's people are under 35.
Kosovo's flag shows a map of the country, like Cyprus.

myths.myth: Kosovo is still a war zone
myths.fact: The war ended in 1999. Today visitors hike, sip coffee and explore old towns.

myths.myth: Kosovo is not a real country
myths.fact: More than 100 countries, including the USA, UK, France and Germany, recognise Kosovo. It belongs to the World Bank.
